overview: This bill expands the official boundary of the Talladega National Forest in Alabama to include land shown on a 2024 Forest Service map. Inside the new boundary, the Agriculture Department, which runs the Forest Service, could acquire land and water through donation, exchange or purchase, but only from willing sellers. Land it acquires would be managed as part of the National Forest System like other national forest land. As of October 27, 2025, a Senate committee had approved it and it was placed on the Senate's calendar, meaning it is eligible for a vote by the full Senate.
for: Supporters say expanding the boundary lets the Forest Service buy land from owners who want to sell, improving conservation and public recreation without forcing anyone to give up property.
against: Critics say adding land to federal ownership can take property off local tax rolls and add to the Forest Service's management costs.
